original_question: For the same landscape-mark model, determine whether spatially non-constant steady states exist in a bounded periodic domain with a top-hat detection kernel, and whether those steady states persist in the local limit R -> 0+.
target_in_paper: Section 2.2.2, Open Problem 7, for the landscape-mark dynamic memory model (2.11).
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the landscape-mark model, the steady-state rather than time-dependent problem, the periodic bounded-domain setting, the top-hat detection kernel, and the local-limit question as R -> 0+. Those are exactly the core ingredients of Open Problem 7.
missing_details: The official target should be named explicitly: Open Problem 7 for model (2.11); the phrase "same landscape-mark model" is not stand-alone.
The unknowns should be stated: u_i(x,t) is the density of population i and p_i(x,t) is the density of marks foreign to population i, for i = 1,...,n.
The governing system should be included: partial_t u_i = d_i Delta u_i - gamma_i div(u_i grad p_{i,g,R}) and partial_t p_i = sum_{j=1}^n alpha_{ij} u_j - mu p_i.
The nearby context defines the perceived mark field through the perception operator: p_{i,g,R}(x,t) = integral over Omega of p_i(y,t) g(x-y) dy, interpreted periodically on the bounded domain.
The top-hat detection function should be defined from (2.3): in one dimension, g_R(z) = 1/(2R) for |z| <= R and 0 otherwise; the paper notes the higher-dimensional norm-based generalization.
The boundary condition should be phrased exactly as periodic boundary conditions on a bounded domain Omega (equivalently, a torus in higher dimensions), not merely as a "bounded periodic domain."

The paper asks "in what sense do spatially non-constant solutions exist," so the solution framework or regularity notion is part of the open problem; the draft currently sounds like a bare yes/no existence question.
The local-limit clause should match the paper's wording: "Do solutions remain well defined in the limit as R -> 0+?" rather than only whether they "persist."
The nearby statement notes that spatially constant steady states are already clear; the open question is specifically about non-constant steady states beyond those.

Algebraic notions such as ambient ring/field, homogeneity degree, or nilpotency are not relevant here; the missing stand-alone data are the PDE variables, operator definitions, kernel, and boundary conditions.
refined_question: For the landscape-mark model (2.11), with unknowns u_i(x,t) (density of population i) and p_i(x,t) (density of marks foreign to population i), i = 1,...,n, given by partial_t u_i = d_i Delta u_i - gamma_i div(u_i grad p_{i,g,R}) and partial_t p_i = sum_{j=1}^n alpha_{ij} u_j - mu p_i on a bounded domain Omega with periodic boundary conditions, where p_{i,g,R}(x) is the periodic spatial convolution of p_i with the top-hat detection kernel g_R from (2.3) (in one dimension, g_R(z) = 1/(2R) for |z| <= R and 0 otherwise), beyond the obvious spatially constant equilibria, in what sense do spatially non-constant periodic steady states (u_i,p_i) exist for the steady-state problem associated to (2.11), and do these steady states remain well defined in the local limit R -> 0+?
justification: The draft is clearly targeting Open Problem 7 in Section 2.2.2, posed immediately after the landscape-mark system (2.11) is introduced. Open Problem 7 asks almost verbatim about spatially non-constant steady states for (2.11) under periodic boundary conditions, a top-hat detection function, and the limit R -> 0+. To make the question fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, one must supply the variables u_i and p_i, the PDE system and perception operator from the surrounding context, the definition of the top-hat kernel from Section 2.1, and the meaning of periodic boundary conditions on a bounded domain from Section 4.1.2. I did not broaden the question to Open Problem 8 (qualitative properties of the non-constant steady states) or Open Problem 9 (other boundary conditions), since the draft does not ask for those.
